message: a way to land on it
$reason: `wrapper-with-aria-and-no-role` with the wrapper kept in by a stop instead of ARIA: a role-less `<div>` between the listbox and an option, `[tabIndex]="-1"` on it. axe's `aria-required-children` looks through a role-less element unless it carries a global ARIA attribute or takes focus, so this one owns the option and a listbox may not own it. Point 9 read the stop off the tree by its literal names — an attribute `tabindex`, an input `tabindex` or `attr.tabindex`, a name the parser never gives one — so the DOM property passed, and so did `TABINDEX`. It reads the same keys as `isFocusable` now.
